semantic_closure.condition: The schedule \(Y\) is fixed before the draw of \(U\), and all probability statements condition on \(Y\).
The coordinates \((U_i)_{i\in I_n}\) are independent \(\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) variables and \(Z_i(r)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le r\}\) for every \(r\in[0,1]\).

semantic_closure.name: Design-computable radius-based variance certificate
semantic_closure.construction: Given the implemented \((p,w)\), compute every reduced covariance block from the known common-uniform kernel and set \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=B^2n^{-1}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}\). The certificate uses the declared radius and the known design, not observed outcomes.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) and stages \(s,t\), \[\operatorname{Cov}_U\!\left(\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(p_s),\prod_{j\in T}Z_j(p_t)\right)=K_{st}(S,T).\] Consequently, \(\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a\) for every low-order schedule.
semantic_closure.justification: This is the first changed proof step relative to spacing envelopes and independent-stage calculations: overlap cardinalities determine every cross-stage term exactly.
semantic_closure.gap: The variance proof of CortezEichhornYu2022 bounds these terms by local overlap and unit magnitudes; it does not state the full subset-intersection kernel.
semantic_closure.consumer: The kernel is the input required by a rollout scheduler to compare candidate ramps using their actual shared-hash dependence.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\sup_{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)}\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{B^2}{n}\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
For every fixed \((p,w)\), if \(v^*\) is a unit leading eigenvector in an active block and \(Q_h\) is its explicit subset-lattice lift, then \(a^*=(B/\sqrt n)\Omega^{1/2}Q_hv^*\) attains the inner supremum. The schedule \(c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S\), \(c^*_{i,\varnothing}=0\), and \(Y_i^*(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c^*_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\) satisfies \(\max_{i\in I_n,z\in\{0,1\}^n}|Y_i^*(z)|\le\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}|a_S^*|<\infty\) and is a legal least-favourable member of \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\). For fixed nodes \(p\), the weight problem has a semidefinite epigraph and attains its value after quotienting the common null directions of the covariance blocks.  The joint node--weight minimum is attained for every declared feasible tuple.
semantic_closure.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it solves Nature's exact common-uniform covariance problem, jointly minimizes over nodes and weights with guaranteed attainment, and produces the required legal converse schedule.
semantic_closure.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 and the accepted Chebyshev-envelope proposal provide upper bounds without an attainable-covariance characterization or a joint-attainment proof; Kallus2021 provides an eigenvalue minimax template but not the nested subset kernel or rollout-node optimization.
semantic_closure.consumer: LinkedIn-style shared-hash ramps obtain a directly computable attained minimum and worst-case precision certificate under a declared interaction-strength budget.

semantic_closure.name: U
semantic_closure.def: \(U=(U_i)_{i\in I_n}\) is the sole source of design randomness.

semantic_closure.name: k
semantic_closure.def: The rollout has \(k+1\) measurements including the baseline and terminal budget fraction.

semantic_closure.name: q
semantic_closure.def: The largest treated fraction observed during the rollout.

semantic_closure.name: delta
semantic_closure.def: The smallest operationally permitted gap between consecutive rollout fractions.

semantic_closure.statement: For every finite \(n\), \(1\le\beta\le n\), positive \(B\), and positive order weights \(\omega\), \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\subsetneq\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}\). Strictness is witnessed by the published-class schedule \(c_{i,\{1\}}=2B\sqrt{\omega_1/n}\) for every \(i\in I_n\), with all other coefficients zero: its nonzero aggregate coefficient satisfies \(a_{\{1\}}=2B\sqrt{\omega_1/n}\) and hence \(a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a=4B^2/n>B^2/n\).
semantic_closure.justification: This records exactly what transfers from the published low-order model and prevents an ellipsoidal achievability result from being presented as a theorem for the full bounded-outcome class.
semantic_closure.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 works with low-order schedules and coefficient-size bounds but does not isolate the permutation-invariant aggregate ellipsoid used by the exact covariance saddle.
semantic_closure.consumer: A reader can identify which parts of the design certificate remain valid when platform-specific coefficient bounds replace the ellipsoid.

semantic_closure.justification: This separates the exact full published schedule-envelope conclusion from the finite-radius ellipsoidal minimax theorem.
semantic_closure.gap: Without an explicit common radius, the broad polynomial schedule union has no finite robust precision guarantee below full rollout.
semantic_closure.consumer: Platform users learn exactly when a coefficient or outcome scale restriction is mathematically necessary for robust rollout design.

semantic_closure.citation: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, and Christina Lee Yu. Staggered Rollout Designs Enable Causal Inference Under Interference Without Network Knowledge. \emph{Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems}, 35, 2022. \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14552}.

Guillaume W. Basse and Edoardo M. Airoldi. Limitations of Design-Based Causal Inference and A/B Testing under Arbitrary and Network Interference. \emph{Sociological Methodology}, 48(1), 2018. \url{https://doi.org/10.1177/0081175018782569}.

semantic_closure.statement: For the schedule in \(\text{def:quadratic-witness}\), \[\Gamma(u,v)=\operatorname{Cov}_U\{M(u),M(v)\}=\frac{\min(u,v)^2-u^2v^2}{9}.\] The nonbaseline interpolation weights are \(w_x=-\{x(1-2x)\}^{-1}\) and \(w_{1/2}=4(1-x)/(1-2x)\), and \[\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{4(1-x)}{9(1-2x)}.\] This risk is strictly increasing on \([1/8,3/8]\), with values \(14/27\) at \(x=1/8\) and \(2/3\) at \(x=1/4\).
semantic_closure.justification: The witness verifies that exact shared-randomizer covariance changes the design criterion and that a familiar interior node need not dominate a more asymmetric node.
semantic_closure.gap: Published rollout bounds do not contain a legal finite-population example with a strict node-risk ordering generated by cross-stage covariance.
semantic_closure.consumer: A design reviewer can use this calculation as a regression test that implementation code has not silently replaced shared-hash stages by independent assignments.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every declared feasible tuple and every \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), define \(r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\).  For every singleton \(S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\),
\[
G(p,w)_{S,S}=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)
\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2
\quad\text{and}\quad
G(p,w)_{S,S}\ge\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
Consequently, if \(0<q<1\), then
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}\ge
\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
At \(q=1\), \(V^*_{n,\beta,k,1,\delta}=0\), attained by \(w_0=-1\), \(w_k=1\), and zero intermediate weights.  If \(\beta=1\), then for every \(0<q\le1\),
\[
V^*_{n,1,k,q,\delta}=\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q},
\]
and, for every fixed feasible \(p\), the unique minimizing weights are \(w_0=-1/q\), \(w_k=1/q\), and \(w_t=0\) for \(0<t<k\).
semantic_closure.justification: This is the sharp rollout-budget obstruction and its exact first-order solution; it also supplies the coercivity needed for joint node--weight attainment.
semantic_closure.gap: Spacing-only envelopes do not expose the exact support restriction induced by a common-uniform ramp or the resulting unique first-order readout.
semantic_closure.consumer: A rollout designer can read off the unavoidable precision loss from stopping at fraction \(q<1\), and can implement the unique optimal first-order weights.

semantic_closure.name: H
semantic_closure.def: \(H_h(p,w)\) is the \(h\)-th diagonal block of \(Q^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}Q\), restricted to the nonempty subset levels.

semantic_closure.name: Exact common-uniform covariance operator
semantic_closure.construction: For \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\), set \(K_{st}(S,T)=\min(p_s,p_t)^{|S\cap T|}p_s^{|S\setminus T|}p_t^{|T\setminus S|}-p_s^{|S|}p_t^{|T|}\) and \(G(p,w)_{S,T}=\sum_{s,t=0}^kw_sw_tK_{st}(S,T)\).

semantic_closure.statement: Because \(\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\) depends on \((S,T)\) only through \((|S|,|T|,|S\cap T|)\), there is an explicit orthogonal subset-lattice transform that block diagonalizes it into isotypic blocks \(H_h(p,w)\), \(h=0,\ldots,\beta\), with block dimension at most \(\beta-h+1\). Each entry of \(H_h(p,w)\) is a finite sum of binomial coefficients and the kernel values \(K_{st}(S,T)\), and \[\lambda_{\max}\{\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\}=\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}.\]
semantic_closure.justification: The reduction converts an operator indexed by all subsets of up to \(\beta\) units into a collection of small matrices without discarding covariance compatibility.
semantic_closure.gap: Neither Kallus2021 nor ChenLiDengWang2023 has the cross-level subset-intersection symmetry created by nested low-order monomials.
semantic_closure.consumer: A platform can evaluate and globally optimize the robust risk for small \(\beta\) without forming a matrix whose dimension grows as \(n^\beta\).

semantic_closure.name: Q
semantic_closure.def: \(Q\) is the explicit orthogonal transform obtained from the harmonic inclusion decomposition of subset levels \(1,\ldots,\beta\); \(Q_h\) denotes its lift for isotypic order \(h\).

semantic_closure.name: u
semantic_closure.def: A generic first scalar rollout fraction.

semantic_closure.name: v
semantic_closure.def: A generic second scalar rollout fraction.

semantic_closure.name: x
semantic_closure.def: The interior rollout fraction in the three-unit quadratic witness.

payload.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}
=\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}
\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w),
\]
and at least one joint minimizer exists.  For every fixed \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), the minimum over \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) is also attained.
payload.proof_tex:
The feasibility conditions give \(k\ge\beta\), \(q>0\), and \(0<\delta\le q/k\).  Hence \(p_t=tq/k\) is feasible.  For any feasible \(p\), the nodes are distinct.  Let \(C(p)\) be the \((\beta+1)\)-by-\((k+1)\) matrix with entries \(C(p)_{d,t}=p_t^d\) for \(0\le d\le\beta\).  A row vector annihilating \(C(p)\) defines a polynomial of degree at most \(\beta\) vanishing at the \(k+1\ge\beta+1\) distinct nodes; it is therefore zero.  Thus \(C(p)\) has full row rank and
\[
C(p)w=(0,1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}
\]
has a solution.  This is precisely an element of \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), so the joint feasible set is nonempty and the infimum is finite.

For a feasible pair define
\[
f(u)=\sum_{t=0}^kw_t\mathbf 1\{u\le p_t\},
\qquad
r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\quad(1\le j\le k).
\]
Degree-one exactness gives
\[
\int_0^1f(u)\,du=\sum_{t=0}^kw_tp_t=1.
\tag{46}
\]
Apart from finitely many endpoints, \(f=r_j\) on \((p_{j-1},p_j]\) and \(f=0\) on \((q,1]\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), the singleton case of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\), and (46) give, for every singleton \(S\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
G(p,w)_{S,S}
&=\operatorname{Var}\{f(U_i)\}\\
&=\int_0^1\{f(u)-1\}^2du\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)\\
&\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{47}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\) and the singleton coordinate Rayleigh quotient therefore imply
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)
\ge\frac{B^2\omega_1\delta}{n}
\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\tag{48}
\]
The multiplier is strictly positive because \(B>0\), \(\omega_1>0\), \(n\ge1\), and \(\delta>0\).

Let \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\) be a joint minimizing sequence.  Its objective values are bounded, so (48) bounds every \(r_j^{(\ell)}\).  The identities
\[
w_k=r_k,
\qquad
w_j=r_j-r_{j+1}\ (1\le j<k),
\qquad
w_0=-r_1
\tag{49}
\]
where the last follows from \(\sum_tw_t=0\), then bound every coordinate of \(w^{(\ell)}\).  The node class is a closed and bounded finite-dimensional polytope, hence compact.  After taking a subsequence, \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\to(p^*,w^*)\).  The endpoint equalities, spacing inequalities, and exactness equations are closed, so the limit is feasible.  The entries of \(G(p,w)\) are continuous because finite sums and products preserve continuity and \((x,y)\mapsto\min(x,y)\) is continuous.  The largest eigenvalue of a finite symmetric matrix is continuous.  Therefore
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^*,w^*)
=\lim_{\ell\to\infty}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})
=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
This proves joint attainment.  With \(p\) fixed, the same argument using (48)--(49) and the closed affine set \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) proves fixed-node attainment.
payload.justification: The first-moment singleton identity makes objective sublevels coercive in the weight coordinates, which turns compactness of the node polytope into joint attainment.
payload.gap: A spectral infimum alone does not certify that an implementable rollout attains it.
payload.consumer: The saddle theorem and the strict higher-order finite-stage barrier both require an attained design.

proposed.name: Published low-order schedule class
proposed.construction:
Let \(E\subseteq I_n\times I_n\) be a static directed graph containing every self-loop and set \(\mathcal N_i(E)=\{j\in I_n:(j,i)\in E\}\).  The noise-free CEY schedule-envelope union is
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}
=\bigcup_{\substack{E\subseteq I_n\times I_n\\(i,i)\in E\ \forall i}}
\left\{(Y,c):
\begin{array}{l}
c_{i,S}=0\text{ whenever }S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\text{ and }S\nsubseteq\mathcal N_i(E),\\
Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal N_i(E)\\|S|\le\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j
\text{ for every }i\in I_n,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
It is the potential-outcome-schedule projection of the published static-graph model after setting observation noise to zero; the union imposes no common bound across schedules.

payload.reason: Define the CEY comparison object as the graph-supported noise-free union and leave its algebraic equivalence to a proved lemma.

payload.tldr: A monotone production ramp assigns unit \(i\) at every fraction by the shared threshold \(Z_i(u)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le u\}\).  Over the declared aggregate-coefficient ellipsoid for a fixed degree-at-most-\(\beta\) schedule, the exact cross-stage covariance is a subset-intersection kernel.  The kernel reduces to small subset-lattice blocks, Nature's worst schedule is an explicit finite-valued leading-eigenvector construction, and the joint node--weight minimum is attained.  Polynomial exactness also yields the degree-sensitive moment barrier \(\Psi_\beta(q)\), which is strictly stronger than the first-moment bound below full rollout when \(\beta\ge2\).  The known-design radius certificate gives finite-sample Chebyshev coverage.  The CEY comparison class is used only as its noise-free union over unknown static graphs: exact covariance and unbiasedness transfer to that union, whereas ellipsoidal minimax equality and radius coverage do not transfer without a common bound.  The sole remaining mathematical gap is a global active-block and node-dual characterization of all minimizers and the Chebyshev--Lobatto win, lose, and tie regions.

project_justification.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 derives unbiased polynomial-interpolation estimators and spacing-based variance bounds under static-neighborhood low-order outcomes, a common-uniform rollout, per-schedule magnitude and neighborhood-size controls, and independent Gaussian observation noise.  It does not retain the full subset-intersection covariance operator, solve the joint exact-covariance node--weight minimax problem, or provide a legal least-favourable schedule for a common robust class.
project_justification.niche: Shared-hash nesting imposes exact compatibility across stages and interaction monomials.  Combining that covariance geometry with all \(\beta\) polynomial moment equations creates a degree-sensitive robust design problem that is neither independent-error polynomial design nor a free positive-semidefinite covariance envelope.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the exact common-uniform kernel, block-diagonalizes its ellipsoidal support operator, proves a jointly attained node--weight spectral minimum, constructs the legal least-favourable schedule, and derives the computable lower barrier \(\Psi_\beta(q)\), including its strict finite-stage gap and small-budget asymptotic.  It also supplies a fixed-design radius variance bound and finite-sample Chebyshev interval.  A global analytic node certificate and the Chebyshev--Lobatto regime map remain open.

sampling_model.design: The paper's design is a noise-free finite-population common-uniform nested Bernoulli rollout: independent \(U_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) variables are drawn once and \(Z_i(p_t)=\mathbf1\{U_i\le p_t\}\) at every stage.  The noisy observation layer in CortezEichhornYu2022 is comparator context, not part of this note's randomization law.

payload.related_work: CortezEichhornYu2022 is the setup and writing anchor.  Its static graph fixes each unit's neighborhood, nonzero low-order coefficients are supported on that neighborhood, interaction degree is bounded, and one common random ordering generates the monotone Bernoulli rollout.  Its finite-schedule bounds use schedule-specific \(Y_{\max}\) and \(L_{\max}\), and its observed responses add independent identically distributed Gaussian noise.  Under the corresponding linear readout, that noise contributes \((\sigma^2/n)\sum_{t=0}^k w_t^2\) in addition to the design variance.  This paper isolates the \(\sigma=0\) potential-outcome projection and takes the union over unknown static graphs.  The complete graph proves that this union is exactly the unrestricted algebraic degree-at-most-\(\beta\) class, so the exact monomial covariance identity and polynomial-exact unbiasedness apply throughout it.  The ellipsoidal minimax equality, leading-eigenvector least-favourable schedule, and radius-based Chebyshev coverage are instead claims only for \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\).  If a genuinely uniform noise-free bound \(\sum_S|c_{i,S}|\le Y_{\max}\) holds and \(\omega_{\min}=\min_d\omega_d\), the algebraic inclusion uses \(B=\sqrt n\,Y_{\max}/\sqrt{\omega_{\min}}\) and yields only a conservative certificate and coverage transfer.  Kallus2021 supplies an ellipsoidal eigenvalue minimax template for two-arm assignment laws, not the nested subset kernel or rollout-node optimization.  ChenLiDengWang2023 optimizes a covariance-based upper bound for a single-stage network estimator, while EichhornKhanUganderYu2024 gives design-dependent low-order variance bounds without the common-uniform cross-stage saddle.  XuChenFernandezSinnoBhasin2015 and LiJamkhandeKochetkovLiu2022 document shared deterministic hashes in production ramps but do not solve the interference-induced cross-threshold design problem.
payload.interpretation: The barrier \(\Psi_\beta(q)\) quantifies the unavoidable extrapolation cost created jointly by the rollout budget and the number of polynomial moments that must be reproduced.  For \(\beta=1\), every feasible node vector with the endpoint readout is optimal.  For \(\beta\ge2\) and \(q<1\), no finite step readout can attain the continuous Riesz-representer relaxation, so the attained exact-covariance optimum lies strictly above the barrier.  At \(q=1\), every node vector is optimal only with the unique endpoint difference readout.
payload.technical_internal_limitation: The permutation-invariant aggregate-coefficient ellipsoid is a strict subclass of the noise-free CEY graph-union schedule envelope.  The unnormalized union has infinite minimax variance whenever \(q<1\); a fixed-radius product-\(\ell^1\) minimax problem remains distinct and open.  A common uniform coefficient bound transfers conservatively into the ellipsoid but need not share its least-favourable schedule, so the transfer is not an exact minimax equivalence.  The finite three-unit witness is a covariance regression test, not a universal node optimum.  The spectral program and existence of minimizers are proved, but a closed-form global node dual and a full Chebyshev--Lobatto phase map are not.
payload.honest_scope: The exact covariance identity and polynomial-exact unbiasedness hold over the complete noise-free CEY graph-union envelope.  Exact minimax equality, the legal leading-eigenvector adversary, the design-computable variance radius, and finite-sample Chebyshev coverage hold only over \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\), with a conservative extension to a uniformly coefficient-bounded subclass through the proved inclusion.  Joint node--weight attainment is established for every declared feasible tuple.  The degree-moment lower barrier is explicit; for \(\beta\ge2\) and \(q<1\), finite-stage strictness shows that it is a relaxation bound rather than the exact optimum.  A design-based central limit theorem is not claimed because the frozen primitives contain no negligible-influence or setwise dependency condition.  The remaining OEQ concerns only a necessary-and-sufficient global active-block/node-dual characterization and the Chebyshev--Lobatto win, lose, and tie regions.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem solves Nature's exact ellipsoidal covariance problem, certifies a legal worst schedule, and proves that the joint node--weight spectral minimum is attained.
statement_notes.gap: The rollout bounds in CortezEichhornYu2022 and the prior Chebyshev-envelope proposal do not characterize an attainable exact covariance adversary or certify universal joint attainment; Kallus2021 does not contain the nested subset kernel or node optimization.
statement_notes.consumer: A shared-hash production ramp obtains a computable attained minimum and a fixed-design worst-case precision certificate under its declared interaction-strength budget.

statement_notes.justification: This is the first design-specific proof step: exact overlap cardinalities determine every cross-stage term under the shared uniform, and the result applies to the entire noise-free CEY graph-union envelope.
statement_notes.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 bounds the relevant cross-stage terms under static-neighborhood magnitude controls; it does not state the full subset-intersection kernel retained here.
statement_notes.consumer: A shared-hash rollout scheduler can compare candidate ramps using their actual nested covariance rather than an independent-stage or spacing envelope.

statement_notes.justification: All \(\beta\) exactness equations produce a degree-sensitive moment barrier, its small-budget law, strict finite-stage separation for higher order, and the complete endpoint characterizations.
statement_notes.gap: Spacing-only bounds retain only the first-moment obstruction and therefore miss both the higher-order growth of \(\Psi_\beta(q)\) and the strict gap between its continuous relaxation and every finite-stage design.
statement_notes.consumer: A rollout designer can quantify the unavoidable budget loss by interaction order, recover the unique first-order endpoint readout, and recognize that the higher-order barrier is not itself a finite-stage optimum.

statement_notes.justification: The exact covariance support function yields an explicit known-design finite-sample interval over the declared ellipsoid, without outcome-estimated variance or a central limit theorem.
statement_notes.gap: Exact covariance and unbiasedness extend to the noise-free CEY graph union, but radius coverage requires the ellipsoid or the separately proved conservative inclusion from a genuinely uniform coefficient bound.

statement_notes.justification: This proposition separates the noise-free CEY graph-union conclusion from both the full noisy fixed-graph model and the finite-radius ellipsoidal saddle.
statement_notes.gap: Without one common coefficient or outcome radius across schedules, the graph-union envelope has no finite robust precision guarantee below full rollout.
statement_notes.consumer: Platform users can see exactly why a common scale restriction is necessary and why schedule-specific bounds in the published model do not create a uniform minimax radius by themselves.

payload.statement:
The noise-free graph-union schedule envelope in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}low\text{-}order\text{-}class}\) equals the unrestricted algebraic degree-at-most-\(\beta\) class:
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}
=\left\{(Y,c):Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+
\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j
\text{ for every }i\in I_n,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n\right\}.
\]
payload.proof_tex:
Let \((Y,c)\) belong to the graph union.  It has a witnessing static directed graph \(E\), every nonzero \(c_{i,S}\) is supported on \(S\subseteq\mathcal N_i(E)\), and every displayed nonempty set has cardinality at most \(\beta\).  Extending the graph-supported sum by the zero off-neighborhood coefficients gives
\[
Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+
\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j.
\]
Thus the graph union is contained in the unrestricted algebraic class.

Conversely, let \((Y,c)\) satisfy the unrestricted algebraic display.  Choose the complete directed graph \(E=I_n\times I_n\).  It contains all self-loops and has \(\mathcal N_i(E)=I_n\) for every \(i\).  Hence every \(S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) is a subset of every \(\mathcal N_i(E)\); no coefficient is excluded by the support condition, and the unrestricted display is exactly the graph-supported expansion in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}low\text{-}order\text{-}class}\).  Therefore \((Y,c)\) belongs to the union.  The two inclusions prove the equality.
payload.justification: The complete graph proves that the noise-free union over unknown static graphs is exactly the unrestricted algebraic low-order schedule class.
payload.gap: The comparison class must distinguish the published fixed-graph noisy model from its noise-free schedule projection.
payload.consumer: The exact covariance theorem, class inclusion, and the unnormalized-envelope witness use the corrected graph-union interpretation without changing their algebra.

payload.statement:
The noise-free graph-union schedule envelope in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}low\text{-}order\text{-}class}\) equals the unrestricted algebraic degree-at-most-\(\beta\) class:
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}
=\left\{(Y,c):Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+
\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j
\text{ for every }i\in I_n,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n\right\}.
\]
payload.proof_tex:
Let \((Y,c)\) belong to the graph union.  It has a witnessing static directed graph \(E\), every nonzero \(c_{i,S}\) is supported on \(S\subseteq\mathcal N_i(E)\), and every displayed nonempty set has cardinality at most \(\beta\).  Extending the graph-supported sum by the zero off-neighborhood coefficients gives
\[
Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+
\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j.
\]
Thus the graph union is contained in the unrestricted algebraic class.

Conversely, let \((Y,c)\) satisfy the unrestricted algebraic display.  Choose the complete directed graph \(E=I_n\times I_n\).  It contains all self-loops and has \(\mathcal N_i(E)=I_n\) for every \(i\).  Hence every \(S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) is a subset of every \(\mathcal N_i(E)\); no coefficient is excluded by the support condition, and the unrestricted display is exactly the graph-supported expansion in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}low\text{-}order\text{-}class}\).  Therefore \((Y,c)\) belongs to the union.  The two inclusions prove the equality.
payload.justification: The complete graph proves that the noise-free union over unknown static graphs is exactly the unrestricted algebraic low-order schedule class.
payload.gap: The comparison class must distinguish the published fixed-graph noisy model from its noise-free schedule projection.
payload.consumer: The exact covariance theorem, class inclusion, and the unnormalized-envelope witness use the corrected graph-union interpretation without changing their algebra.

payload.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}
=\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}
\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w),
\]
and at least one joint minimizer exists.  For every fixed \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), the minimum over \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) is also attained.
payload.proof_tex:
The feasibility conditions give \(k\ge\beta\), \(q>0\), and \(0<\delta\le q/k\).  Hence \(p_t=tq/k\) is feasible.  For any feasible \(p\), the nodes are distinct.  Let \(C(p)\) be the \((\beta+1)\)-by-\((k+1)\) matrix with entries \(C(p)_{d,t}=p_t^d\) for \(0\le d\le\beta\).  A row vector annihilating \(C(p)\) defines a polynomial of degree at most \(\beta\) vanishing at the \(k+1\ge\beta+1\) distinct nodes; it is therefore zero.  Thus \(C(p)\) has full row rank and
\[
C(p)w=(0,1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}
\]
has a solution.  This is precisely an element of \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), so the joint feasible set is nonempty and the infimum is finite.

For a feasible pair define
\[
f(u)=\sum_{t=0}^kw_t\mathbf 1\{u\le p_t\},
\qquad
r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\quad(1\le j\le k).
\]
Degree-one exactness gives
\[
\int_0^1f(u)\,du=\sum_{t=0}^kw_tp_t=1.
\tag{46}
\]
Apart from finitely many endpoints, \(f=r_j\) on \((p_{j-1},p_j]\) and \(f=0\) on \((q,1]\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), the singleton case of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\), and (46) give, for every singleton \(S\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
G(p,w)_{S,S}
&=\operatorname{Var}\{f(U_i)\}\\
&=\int_0^1\{f(u)-1\}^2du\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)\\
&\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{47}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\) and the singleton coordinate Rayleigh quotient therefore imply
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)
\ge\frac{B^2\omega_1\delta}{n}
\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\tag{48}
\]
The multiplier is strictly positive because \(B>0\), \(\omega_1>0\), \(n\ge1\), and \(\delta>0\).

Let \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\) be a joint minimizing sequence.  Its objective values are bounded, so (48) bounds every \(r_j^{(\ell)}\).  The identities
\[
w_k=r_k,
\qquad
w_j=r_j-r_{j+1}\ (1\le j<k),
\qquad
w_0=-r_1
\tag{49}
\]
where the last follows from \(\sum_tw_t=0\), then bound every coordinate of \(w^{(\ell)}\).  The node class is a closed and bounded finite-dimensional polytope, hence compact.  After taking a subsequence, \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\to(p^*,w^*)\).  The endpoint equalities, spacing inequalities, and exactness equations are closed, so the limit is feasible.  The entries of \(G(p,w)\) are continuous because finite sums and products preserve continuity and \((x,y)\mapsto\min(x,y)\) is continuous.  The largest eigenvalue of a finite symmetric matrix is continuous.  Therefore
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^*,w^*)
=\lim_{\ell\to\infty}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})
=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
This proves joint attainment.  With \(p\) fixed, the same argument using (48)--(49) and the closed affine set \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) proves fixed-node attainment.
payload.justification: The first-moment singleton identity makes objective sublevels coercive in the weight coordinates, which turns compactness of the node polytope into joint attainment.
payload.gap: A spectral infimum alone does not certify that an implementable rollout attains it.
payload.consumer: The saddle theorem and the strict higher-order finite-stage barrier both require an attained design.

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix a declared feasible tuple.  Every \(\omega_d\) is positive, so \(\Omega\) is positive definite.  For a fixed feasible \((p,w)\), put
\[
A(p,w)=\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2},
\qquad b=\Omega^{-1/2}a.
\]
Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}aggregate\text{-}coefficient\text{-}ellipsoid}\) is exactly
\[
\|b\|_2^2=a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le\frac{B^2}{n}.
\tag{65}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a=b^{\mathsf T}A(p,w)b.
\tag{66}
\]
The matrix \(A(p,w)\) is positive semidefinite: for any real aggregate vector \(a\), take the fixed array \(c_{i,S}=a_S\), \(c_{i,\varnothing}=0\); then the right side of (66) is a variance.  Expanding a vector in an orthonormal eigenbasis of the finite symmetric matrix gives
\[
\sup_{\|b\|_2^2\le B^2/n}b^{\mathsf T}A(p,w)b
=\frac{B^2}{n}\lambda_{\max}\{A(p,w)\}.
\tag{67}
\]

The supremum is attained by a legal schedule.  By Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\), choose an active block \(h\), a unit leading eigenvector \(v^*\) of \(H_h(p,w)\), and its unit orthogonal lift \(Q_hv^*\).  Set
\[
a^*=\frac B{\sqrt n}\Omega^{1/2}Q_hv^*.
\tag{68}
\]
Orthogonality gives
\[
(a^*)^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a^*=\frac{B^2}{n},
\qquad
(a^*)^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a^*
=\frac{B^2}{n}\lambda_{\max}\{A(p,w)\}.
\tag{69}
\]
For every \(i\in I_n\), define
\[
c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S,
\qquad c^*_{i,\varnothing}=0,
\qquad
Y_i^*(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a^*_S\prod_{j\in S}z_j.
\tag{70}
\]
This array is fixed before \(U\) by Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}finite\text{-}population}\), and it has degree at most \(\beta\) by Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}low\text{-}order\text{-}schedule}\).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}cey\text{-}envelope\text{-}union\text{-}equivalence}\), whose reverse inclusion uses the complete directed graph, places (70) in the corrected noise-free graph-union envelope.  Its aggregate coefficient is \(a^*\), and (69) verifies the ellipsoid condition.  Finally, finiteness of \(n\) and \(\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) gives
\[
\max_{i\in I_n,\ z\in\{0,1\}^n}|Y_i^*(z)|
\le\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}|a_S^*|<\infty.
\tag{71}
\]
Thus (70) is a legal least-favourable member of \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\) and attains (67).

Combining (66)--(71), Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\), and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}variance\text{-}certificate}\) gives, for every fixed feasible pair,
\[
\sup_{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)}
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=\frac{B^2}{n}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}
=V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w).
\tag{72}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}joint\text{-}design\text{-}attainment}\) and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}saddle}\) replace both infima in (72) by attained minima.  This proves the headline equality and universal joint attainment.

It remains to expose the fixed-node semidefinite epigraph.  Let \(d_\beta=|\mathcal S_{n,\beta}|\), and let \(\mathbb K(p)\) be indexed by pairs \((s,S)\), with block entry \(K_{st}(S,T)\).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\) identifies \(\mathbb K(p)\) as a covariance matrix, so \(\mathbb K(p)\succeq0\).  Define
\[
D_p(w)b=(w_0\Omega^{1/2}b,\ldots,w_k\Omega^{1/2}b)^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
L_p(w)=\mathbb K(p)^{1/2}D_p(w).
\]
Direct block multiplication gives
\[
A(p,w)=D_p(w)^{\mathsf T}\mathbb K(p)D_p(w)
=L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}L_p(w).
\tag{73}
\]
With \(C(p)_{r,t}=p_t^r\) for \(0\le r\le\beta\) and \(e=(0,1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}\), the weight constraints are \(C(p)w=e\).  Completing the square gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\rho I_{d_\beta}&L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}\\
L_p(w)&I_{(k+1)d_\beta}
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\rho I_{d_\beta}-L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}L_p(w)\succeq0,
\tag{74}
\]
because the quadratic form at \((x,y)\) equals
\[
x^{\mathsf T}\{\rho I_{d_\beta}-L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}L_p(w)\}x
+\|y+L_p(w)x\|_2^2.
\]
Thus the fixed-node weight problem is the explicit semidefinite program
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{minimize}_{w,\rho}&\rho\\
\text{subject to}&C(p)w=e,\\
&\begin{pmatrix}
\rho I_{d_\beta}&L_p(w)^{\mathsf T}\\
L_p(w)&I_{(k+1)d_\beta}
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\end{array}
\tag{75}
\]
Its entries are affine in \((w,\rho)\), and (73)--(74) show that its value is \(\lambda_{\max}\{A(p,w)\}\).  It descends to the quotient by the common null space \(\mathcal N_p=\ker\{w\mapsto L_p(w)\}\), because the objective is constant on its cosets.  Fixed-node attainment follows from Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}joint\text{-}design\text{-}attainment}\).  This proves the semidefinite-epigraph and attainment assertions without claiming the still-open global node dual characterization.

target_declaration.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\sup_{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)}\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{B^2}{n}\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
For every fixed \((p,w)\), if \(v^*\) is a unit leading eigenvector in an active block and \(Q_h\) is its explicit subset-lattice lift, then \(a^*=(B/\sqrt n)\Omega^{1/2}Q_hv^*\) attains the inner supremum. The schedule \(c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S\), \(c^*_{i,\varnothing}=0\), and \(Y_i^*(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c^*_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\) satisfies \(\max_{i\in I_n,z\in\{0,1\}^n}|Y_i^*(z)|\le\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}|a_S^*|<\infty\) and is a legal least-favourable member of \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\). For fixed nodes \(p\), the weight problem has a semidefinite epigraph and attains its value after quotienting the common null directions of the covariance blocks.  The joint node--weight minimum is attained for every declared feasible tuple.
target_declaration.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it solves Nature's exact common-uniform covariance problem, jointly minimizes over nodes and weights with guaranteed attainment, and produces the required legal converse schedule.
target_declaration.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 and the accepted Chebyshev-envelope proposal provide upper bounds without an attainable-covariance characterization or a joint-attainment proof; Kallus2021 provides an eigenvalue minimax template but not the nested subset kernel or rollout-node optimization.
target_declaration.consumer: LinkedIn-style shared-hash ramps obtain a directly computable attained minimum and worst-case precision certificate under a declared interaction-strength budget.

semantic_closure.condition: The schedule \(Y\) is fixed before the draw of \(U\), and all probability statements condition on \(Y\).
The coordinates \((U_i)_{i\in I_n}\) are independent \(\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) variables and \(Z_i(r)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le r\}\) for every \(r\in[0,1]\).
For every \(i\in I_n\) and \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\).
The aggregate coefficient vector satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le B^2/n\).

novel.justification: This permutation-invariant energy restriction models platforms with many weak interactions whose root-mean-square aggregate strength is stable within each interaction order. It contains dense exchangeable spillovers, sparse local interactions, and mixtures across every order up to \(\beta\), while allowing the order weights to be calibrated from domain bounds or a pilot ramp.

semantic_closure.name: Ellipsoidal common-uniform coefficient class
semantic_closure.construction: \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)=\{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{CEY}}_{n,\beta}:a_S=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_n}c_{i,S}\text{ for every }S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta},\ a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le B^2/n\}\).

semantic_closure.name: Exact common-uniform covariance operator
semantic_closure.construction: For \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\), set \(K_{st}(S,T)=\min(p_s,p_t)^{|S\cap T|}p_s^{|S\setminus T|}p_t^{|T\setminus S|}-p_s^{|S|}p_t^{|T|}\) and \(G(p,w)_{S,T}=\sum_{s,t=0}^kw_sw_tK_{st}(S,T)\).

semantic_closure.name: Design-computable radius-based variance certificate
semantic_closure.construction: Given the implemented \((p,w)\), compute every reduced covariance block from the known common-uniform kernel and set \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=B^2n^{-1}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}\). The certificate uses the declared radius and the known design, not observed outcomes.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) and stages \(s,t\), \[\operatorname{Cov}_U\!\left(\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(p_s),\prod_{j\in T}Z_j(p_t)\right)=K_{st}(S,T).\] Consequently, \(\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a\) for every low-order schedule.
semantic_closure.justification: This is the first changed proof step relative to spacing envelopes and independent-stage calculations: overlap cardinalities determine every cross-stage term exactly.
semantic_closure.gap: The variance proof of CortezEichhornYu2022 bounds these terms by local overlap and unit magnitudes; it does not state the full subset-intersection kernel.
semantic_closure.consumer: The kernel is the input required by a rollout scheduler to compare candidate ramps using their actual shared-hash dependence.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) and write
\[
X_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(r).
\]
By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), the coordinates of \(U\) are independent and \(\Pr_U(U_i\le r)=r\).  Hence
\[
\mathbb E_U X_S(p_s)=p_s^{|S|}.
\]
For a coordinate in \(S\cap T\),
\[
\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_s\}\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_t\}
=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le\min(p_s,p_t)\}.
\]
Coordinates in \(S\setminus T\) and \(T\setminus S\) occur at only one stage.  Independence across coordinates therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E_U\{X_S(p_s)X_T(p_t)\}
=\min(p_s,p_t)^{|S\cap T|}p_s^{|S\setminus T|}p_t^{|T\setminus S|}.
\]
Subtracting \(\mathbb E_U X_S(p_s)\mathbb E_U X_T(p_t)=p_s^{|S|}p_t^{|T|}\) proves the displayed covariance formula, which is \(K_{st}(S,T)\) by Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}covariance\text{-}operator}\).

By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}low\text{-}order\text{-}schedule}\) and the definition of \(a\), finite summation over units yields
\[
M(r)=\bar c_{\varnothing}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_SX_S(r),
\qquad
\bar c_{\varnothing}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}c_{i,\varnothing}.
\]
Consequently, Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}rollout\text{-}estimator}\) gives
\[
\widehat\tau_{p,w}
=\bar c_{\varnothing}\sum_{t=0}^kw_t
+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_S\sum_{t=0}^kw_tX_S(p_t).
\]
The first term is nonrandom.  Bilinearity of covariance, the monomial identity just proved, and finiteness of \(\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
&=\sum_{S,T}a_Sa_T\sum_{s,t=0}^kw_sw_tK_{st}(S,T)\\
&=\sum_{S,T}a_SG(p,w)_{S,T}a_T
=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second equality is Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}covariance\text{-}operator}\).  This proves both claims.

semantic_closure.statement: Because \(\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\) depends on \((S,T)\) only through \((|S|,|T|,|S\cap T|)\), there is an explicit orthogonal subset-lattice transform that block diagonalizes it into isotypic blocks \(H_h(p,w)\), \(h=0,\ldots,\beta\), with block dimension at most \(\beta-h+1\). Each entry of \(H_h(p,w)\) is a finite sum of binomial coefficients and the kernel values \(K_{st}(S,T)\), and \[\lambda_{\max}\{\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\}=\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}.\]
semantic_closure.justification: The reduction converts an operator indexed by all subsets of up to \(\beta\) units into a collection of small matrices without discarding covariance compatibility.
semantic_closure.gap: Neither Kallus2021 nor ChenLiDengWang2023 has the cross-level subset-intersection symmetry created by nested low-order monomials.
semantic_closure.consumer: A platform can evaluate and globally optimize the robust risk for small \(\beta\) without forming a matrix whose dimension grows as \(n^\beta\).
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Put \(\mathcal X_r=\{S\subseteq I_n:|S|=r\}\).  For \(0\le j\le r\le n\), let \(R_{rj}\) be the inclusion matrix with rows indexed by \(\mathcal X_r\), columns indexed by \(\mathcal X_j\), and entries
\[
(R_{rj})_{S,A}=\mathbf 1\{A\subseteq S\}.
\]
For every admissible \(r,\ell,j\), direct counting gives
\[
(R_{rj}R_{\ell j}^{\mathsf T})_{S,T}=\binom{|S\cap T|}{j}.
\tag{1}
\]

Define the down operator \(D_j=R_{j,j-1}^{\mathsf T}\), the up operator \(U_j=R_{j+1,j}\), and
\[
\mathcal L_0=\mathbb R,
\qquad
\mathcal L_h=\ker(D_h)\quad(h\ge1).
\]
If \(g\) is a function on \(\mathcal X_j\), counting separately the term that leaves a set unchanged and the terms that exchange one element proves
\[
D_{j+1}U_jg-U_{j-1}D_jg=(n-2j)g.
\tag{2}
\]
Iterating (2) gives, for \(0\le h\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), \(g_1,g_2\in\mathcal L_h\), and \(h\le r\le n-h\),
\[
\langle R_{rh}g_1,R_{rh}g_2\rangle
=\binom{n-2h}{r-h}\langle g_1,g_2\rangle,
\tag{3}
\]
and the lifted spaces arising from distinct \(h\)'s are orthogonal.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb R^{\mathcal X_r}
=\bigoplus_{h=0}^{\min(r,n-r)}R_{rh}\mathcal L_h.
\tag{4}
\]
For completeness, taking the inner product of (2) with a vector in \(\ker D_j\) gives injectivity of \(U_j\) when \(j<n/2\) and the squared-norm multiplier \(n-2j\).  Successive application from level \(h\) to level \(r\), together with \(R_{rh}=U_{r-1}\cdots U_h/(r-h)!\), proves (3).  Moving down operators to the other side of an inner product proves orthogonality because they annihilate the harmonic vector.  Finally, rank--nullity gives \(\dim\mathcal L_h=\binom nh-\binom n{h-1}\); summing over \(h\le\min(r,n-r)\) gives \(\binom nr\), proving (4).

Choose an orthonormal basis \(e_{h,1},\ldots,e_{h,d_h}\) of each \(\mathcal L_h\), where \(d_h=\dim\mathcal L_h\).  By (3)--(4), the vectors
\[
q_{r,h,j}
=\binom{n-2h}{r-h}^{-1/2}R_{rh}e_{h,j},
\qquad
h\le r\le\min(\beta,n-h),
\tag{5}
\]
over all admissible \((r,h,j)\), form an orthonormal basis of the direct sum of the nonempty subset levels \(1,\ldots,\beta\).  Thus (5) constructs the orthogonal transform \(Q\) from finite incidence matrices and orthonormal bases of explicit null spaces.

Set
\[
A=\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}.
\]
By Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}covariance\text{-}operator}\), \(G(p,w)_{S,T}\) depends on \((S,T)\) only through \((|S|,|T|,|S\cap T|)\); multiplication by \(\Omega^{1/2}\), whose diagonal entry on level \(r\) is \(\sqrt{\omega_r}\), preserves this property.  Hence the level-\((r,\ell)\) block of \(A\) has entries \(\phi_{r\ell}(|S\cap T|)\) for an explicit function \(\phi_{r\ell}\).  If \((\Delta h)(c)=h(c+1)-h(c)\), the finite Newton expansion
\[
\phi_{r\ell}(c)
=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(r,\ell)}(\Delta^j\phi_{r\ell})(0)\binom cj
\tag{6}
\]
and (1) express this level block as a finite linear combination of \(R_{rj}R_{\ell j}^{\mathsf T}\).

If \(g\in\mathcal L_h\), repeated use of (2), or direct counting followed by \(D_hg=0\), gives
\[
R_{\ell j}^{\mathsf T}R_{\ell h}g
=\begin{cases}
0,&j<h,\\
\displaystyle\binom{n-h-j}{\ell-j}R_{jh}g,&h\le j\le\ell.
\end{cases}
\tag{7}
\]
For the second coefficient, use \(R_{\ell j}R_{jh}=\binom{\ell-h}{j-h}R_{\ell h}\), take the inner product with \(R_{jh}g\), and apply (3); the resulting ratio is
\[
\frac{\binom{\ell-h}{j-h}\binom{n-2h}{\ell-h}}
{\binom{n-2h}{j-h}}
=\binom{n-h-j}{\ell-j}.
\]
Writing \(\gamma_{r\ell j}=(\Delta^j\phi_{r\ell})(0)\), equations (6)--(7) and \(R_{rj}R_{jh}=\binom{r-h}{j-h}R_{rh}\) yield
\[
A_{r\ell}R_{\ell h}g
=\left\{
\sum_{j=h}^{\min(r,\ell)}
\gamma_{r\ell j}
\binom{n-h-j}{\ell-j}
\binom{r-h}{j-h}
\right\}R_{rh}g.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus every matrix in (6) preserves harmonic order and acts independently of the harmonic basis index; distinct harmonic orders are orthogonal by (4).  Therefore \(Q^{\mathsf T}AQ\) is block diagonal.  For fixed \(h\), its nonzero level coordinates are indexed by
\[
\mathcal R_h=\{r:1\le r\le\beta,\ h\le r\le n-h\},
\]
so the block \(H_h(p,w)\) has size \(|\mathcal R_h|\le\beta-h+1\) and is repeated \(d_h\) times; absent coordinates may be padded by zero rows and columns.  Equations (1), (5), and (8) show that each entry is a finite sum of binomial coefficients and quantities
\[
\sqrt{\omega_r\omega_\ell}\sum_{s,t=0}^kw_sw_tK_{st}(S,T).
\]
Orthogonal similarity preserves eigenvalues, and repetitions do not change their maximum.  Hence
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A)
=\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\},
\]
which proves the lemma.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every declared feasible tuple and every \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), define \(r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\).  For every singleton \(S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\),
\[
G(p,w)_{S,S}=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)
\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2
\quad\text{and}\quad
G(p,w)_{S,S}\ge\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
Consequently, if \(0<q<1\), then
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}\ge
\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
At \(q=1\), \(V^*_{n,\beta,k,1,\delta}=0\), attained by \(w_0=-1\), \(w_k=1\), and zero intermediate weights.  If \(\beta=1\), then for every \(0<q\le1\),
\[
V^*_{n,1,k,q,\delta}=\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q},
\]
and, for every fixed feasible \(p\), the unique minimizing weights are \(w_0=-1/q\), \(w_k=1/q\), and \(w_t=0\) for \(0<t<k\).
semantic_closure.justification: This is the sharp rollout-budget obstruction and its exact first-order solution; it also supplies the coercivity needed for joint node--weight attainment.
semantic_closure.gap: Spacing-only envelopes do not expose the exact support restriction induced by a common-uniform ramp or the resulting unique first-order readout.
semantic_closure.consumer: A rollout designer can read off the unavoidable precision loss from stopping at fraction \(q<1\), and can implement the unique optimal first-order weights.

semantic_closure.statement: For every \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), and \((Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\), \[\mathbb E_U[\widehat\tau_{p,w}]=\tau,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})\le V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w).\] If \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)>0\), then for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \[\Pr_U\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_{p,w}-\tau|\le\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)/\alpha}\right\}\ge1-\alpha,\] equivalently \(\Pr_U\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}^{\mathrm{Ch}}_{1-\alpha}(p,w)\}\ge1-\alpha\). If \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{p,w}=\tau\) almost surely and the singleton interval \(\{\widehat\tau_{p,w}\}\) has coverage one.

semantic_closure.citation: Guillaume W. Basse and Edoardo M. Airoldi. Limitations of Design-Based Causal Inference and A/B Testing under Arbitrary and Network Interference. \emph{Sociological Methodology}, 48(1), 2018. \url{https://doi.org/10.1177/0081175018782569}.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}
=\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}
\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w),
\]
and at least one joint minimizer exists.  For every fixed \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), the minimum over \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) is also attained.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The feasibility conditions give \(k\ge\beta\), \(q>0\), and \(0<\delta\le q/k\).  Hence \(p_t=tq/k\) is feasible.  For any feasible \(p\), the nodes are distinct.  Let \(C(p)\) be the \((\beta+1)\)-by-\((k+1)\) matrix with entries \(C(p)_{d,t}=p_t^d\) for \(0\le d\le\beta\).  A row vector annihilating \(C(p)\) defines a polynomial of degree at most \(\beta\) vanishing at the \(k+1\ge\beta+1\) distinct nodes; it is therefore zero.  Thus \(C(p)\) has full row rank and
\[
C(p)w=(0,1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}
\]
has a solution.  This is precisely an element of \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), so the joint feasible set is nonempty and the infimum is finite.

For a feasible pair define
\[
f(u)=\sum_{t=0}^kw_t\mathbf 1\{u\le p_t\},
\qquad
r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\quad(1\le j\le k).
\]
Degree-one exactness gives
\[
\int_0^1f(u)\,du=\sum_{t=0}^kw_tp_t=1.
\tag{46}
\]
Apart from finitely many endpoints, \(f=r_j\) on \((p_{j-1},p_j]\) and \(f=0\) on \((q,1]\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), the singleton case of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\), and (46) give, for every singleton \(S\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
G(p,w)_{S,S}
&=\operatorname{Var}\{f(U_i)\}\\
&=\int_0^1\{f(u)-1\}^2du\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)\\
&\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{47}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\) and the singleton coordinate Rayleigh quotient therefore imply
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)
\ge\frac{B^2\omega_1\delta}{n}
\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\tag{48}
\]
The multiplier is strictly positive because \(B>0\), \(\omega_1>0\), \(n\ge1\), and \(\delta>0\).

Let \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\) be a joint minimizing sequence.  Its objective values are bounded, so (48) bounds every \(r_j^{(\ell)}\).  The identities
\[
w_k=r_k,
\qquad
w_j=r_j-r_{j+1}\ (1\le j<k),
\qquad
w_0=-r_1
\tag{49}
\]
where the last follows from \(\sum_tw_t=0\), then bound every coordinate of \(w^{(\ell)}\).  The node class is a closed and bounded finite-dimensional polytope, hence compact.  After taking a subsequence, \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\to(p^*,w^*)\).  The endpoint equalities, spacing inequalities, and exactness equations are closed, so the limit is feasible.  The entries of \(G(p,w)\) are continuous because finite sums and products preserve continuity and \((x,y)\mapsto\min(x,y)\) is continuous.  The largest eigenvalue of a finite symmetric matrix is continuous.  Therefore
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^*,w^*)
=\lim_{\ell\to\infty}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})
=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
This proves joint attainment.  With \(p\) fixed, the same argument using (48)--(49) and the closed affine set \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) proves fixed-node attainment.
semantic_closure.justification: The first-moment singleton identity makes objective sublevels coercive in the weight coordinates, which turns compactness of the node polytope into joint attainment.
semantic_closure.gap: A spectral infimum alone does not certify that an implementable rollout attains it.
semantic_closure.consumer: The saddle theorem and the strict higher-order finite-stage barrier both require an attained design.

semantic_closure.statement: For the schedule in \(\text{def:quadratic-witness}\), \[\Gamma(u,v)=\operatorname{Cov}_U\{M(u),M(v)\}=\frac{\min(u,v)^2-u^2v^2}{9}.\] The nonbaseline interpolation weights are \(w_x=-\{x(1-2x)\}^{-1}\) and \(w_{1/2}=4(1-x)/(1-2x)\), and \[\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{4(1-x)}{9(1-2x)}.\] This risk is strictly increasing on \([1/8,3/8]\), with values \(14/27\) at \(x=1/8\) and \(2/3\) at \(x=1/4\).
semantic_closure.justification: The witness verifies that exact shared-randomizer covariance changes the design criterion and that a familiar interior node need not dominate a more asymmetric node.
semantic_closure.gap: Published rollout bounds do not contain a legal finite-population example with a strict node-risk ordering generated by cross-stage covariance.
semantic_closure.consumer: A design reviewer can use this calculation as a regression test that implementation code has not silently replaced shared-hash stages by independent assignments.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Under Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}quadratic\text{-}witness}\),
\[
M(r)=\frac13Z_1(r)Z_2(r).
\]
By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), or by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\) with \(S=T=\{1,2\}\),
\[
\Gamma(u,v)=\frac19\{\min(u,v)^2-u^2v^2\}.
\tag{35}
\]
Let the weights at \(x\) and \(1/2\) be \(w_x\) and \(w_{1/2}\).  The degree-one and degree-two equations in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}unbiased\text{-}weight\text{-}class}\) are
\[
xw_x+\frac12w_{1/2}=1,
\qquad
x^2w_x+\frac14w_{1/2}=1.
\]
Their determinant is \(x(1-2x)/4>0\) for \(x\in[1/8,3/8]\), so their unique solution is
\[
w_x=-\frac1{x(1-2x)},
\qquad
w_{1/2}=\frac{4(1-x)}{1-2x}.
\tag{36}
\]
The remaining equation fixes \(w_0=-w_x-w_{1/2}\); it contributes no random term because \(M(0)=0\).

Using (35) at the three required pairs gives
\[
9\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=w_x^2(x^2-x^4)
+2w_xw_{1/2}\frac{3x^2}{4}
+w_{1/2}^2\frac3{16}.
\]
Substitution of (36) and collection over \((1-2x)^2\) give
\[
9\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=\frac{1-x^2-6x(1-x)+3(1-x)^2}{(1-2x)^2}
=\frac{4(1-x)}{1-2x}.
\]
Its derivative is
\[
\frac{d}{dx}\frac{4(1-x)}{9(1-2x)}
=\frac4{9(1-2x)^2}>0,
\]
so the risk is strictly increasing.  Direct evaluation gives \(14/27\) at \(x=1/8\) and \(2/3\) at \(x=1/4\), proving the proposition and verifying the smallest-instance common-uniform arithmetic.

semantic_closure.citation: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, and Christina Lee Yu. Staggered Rollout Designs Enable Causal Inference Under Interference Without Network Knowledge. \emph{Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems}, 35, 2022. \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14552}.

proposed.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\sup_{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)}\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{B^2}{n}\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
For every fixed \((p,w)\), if \(v^*\) is a unit leading eigenvector in an active block and \(Q_h\) is its explicit subset-lattice lift, then \(a^*=(B/\sqrt n)\Omega^{1/2}Q_hv^*\) attains the inner supremum. The schedule \(c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S\), \(c^*_{i,\varnothing}=0\), and \(Y_i^*(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c^*_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\) satisfies \(\max_{i\in I_n,z\in\{0,1\}^n}|Y_i^*(z)|\le\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}|a_S^*|<\infty\) and is a legal least-favourable member of \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\). For fixed nodes \(p\), the weight problem has a semidefinite epigraph and attains its value after quotienting the common null directions of the covariance blocks.  The joint node--weight minimum is attained for every declared feasible tuple.
proposed.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it solves Nature's exact common-uniform covariance problem, jointly minimizes over nodes and weights with guaranteed attainment, and produces the required legal converse schedule.
proposed.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 and the accepted Chebyshev-envelope proposal provide upper bounds without an attainable-covariance characterization or a joint-attainment proof; Kallus2021 provides an eigenvalue minimax template but not the nested subset kernel or rollout-node optimization.
proposed.consumer: LinkedIn-style shared-hash ramps obtain a directly computable attained minimum and worst-case precision certificate under a declared interaction-strength budget.

payload.justification: This theorem solves Nature's exact ellipsoidal covariance problem, certifies a legal worst schedule, and proves that the joint node--weight spectral minimum is attained.
payload.gap: The rollout bounds in CortezEichhornYu2022 and the prior Chebyshev-envelope proposal do not characterize an attainable exact covariance adversary or certify universal joint attainment; Kallus2021 does not contain the nested subset kernel or node optimization.

carrier.proof_tex:
Fix a feasible \((p,w)\) and a schedule in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}ellipsoidal\text{-}coefficient\text{-}class}\).  The low-order expansion and Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\) give
\[
\mathbb E_U M(r)=\bar c_{\varnothing}
+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_Sr^{|S|}.
\tag{37}
\]
By Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}unbiased\text{-}weight\text{-}class}\), \(\sum_tw_t=0\) and \(\sum_tw_tp_t^d=1\) for \(1\le d\le\beta\).  Applying these equations term by term in (37) yields
\[
\mathbb E_U\widehat\tau_{p,w}=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_S.
\tag{38}
\]
Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}low\text{-}order\text{-}schedule}\) separately gives the causal contrast
\[
\tau=\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}\{Y_i(\mathbf1)-Y_i(\mathbf0)\}
=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_S.
\tag{39}
\]
Thus (38)--(39) prove design unbiasedness rather than defining it.

Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a.
\]
Since every \(\omega_d>0\), set \(b=\Omega^{-1/2}a\).  The ellipsoid assumption gives \(\|b\|_2^2\le B^2/n\), and the Rayleigh inequality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a
&=b^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}b\\
&\le\frac{B^2}{n}\lambda_{\max}\{\Omega^{1/2}G(p,w)\Omega^{1/2}\}\\
&=V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w),
\end{aligned}
\tag{40}
\]
where the last equality uses Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\) and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}variance\text{-}certificate}\).

Suppose \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)>0\), put \(X=\widehat\tau_{p,w}-\tau\), and set \(R=\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)/\alpha}\).  Equations (38)--(40) give \(\mathbb E_UX=0\) and \(\mathbb E_UX^2\le V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)\).  The pointwise inequality
\[
X^2\ge R^2\mathbf1\{|X|>R\}
\]
implies
\[
\Pr_U(|X|>R)\le\frac{\mathbb E_UX^2}{R^2}\le\alpha.
\]
Taking complements and using Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}chebyshev\text{-}interval}\) proves the coverage claim.  If \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=0\), (40) gives \(\mathbb E_UX^2=0\); nonnegativity of \(X^2\) implies \(X=0\) almost surely.  The singleton interval therefore covers with probability one.

If \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{p,w}=\tau\) almost surely and the singleton interval \(\{\widehat\tau_{p,w}\}\) has coverage one.

semantic_closure.condition: The schedule \(Y\) is fixed before the draw of \(U\), and all probability statements condition on \(Y\).
The coordinates \((U_i)_{i\in I_n}\) are independent \(\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) variables and \(Z_i(r)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le r\}\) for every \(r\in[0,1]\).
For every \(i\in I_n\) and \(z\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(Y_i(z)=c_{i,\varnothing}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\).
The aggregate coefficient vector satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}\Omega^{-1}a\le B^2/n\).

novel.justification: This permutation-invariant energy restriction models platforms with many weak interactions whose root-mean-square aggregate strength is stable within each interaction order. It contains dense exchangeable spillovers, sparse local interactions, and mixtures across every order up to \(\beta\), while allowing the order weights to be calibrated from domain bounds or a pilot ramp.

semantic_closure.construction: Given the implemented \((p,w)\), compute every reduced covariance block from the known common-uniform kernel and set \(V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)=B^2n^{-1}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}\). semantic_closure.statement: For every \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) and stages \(s,t\), \[\operatorname{Cov}_U\!\left(\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(p_s),\prod_{j\in T}Z_j(p_t)\right)=K_{st}(S,T).\] Consequently, \(\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a\) for every low-order schedule.
semantic_closure.justification: This is the first changed proof step relative to spacing envelopes and independent-stage calculations: overlap cardinalities determine every cross-stage term exactly.
semantic_closure.gap: The variance proof of CortezEichhornYu2022 bounds these terms by local overlap and unit magnitudes; it does not state the full subset-intersection kernel.
semantic_closure.consumer: The kernel is the input required by a rollout scheduler to compare candidate ramps using their actual shared-hash dependence.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(S,T\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) and write
\[
X_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(r).
\]
By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), the coordinates of \(U\) are independent and \(\Pr_U(U_i\le r)=r\).  Hence
\[
\mathbb E_U X_S(p_s)=p_s^{|S|}.
\]
For a coordinate in \(S\cap T\),
\[
\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_s\}\mathbf 1\{U_i\le p_t\}
=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le\min(p_s,p_t)\}.
\]
Coordinates in \(S\setminus T\) and \(T\setminus S\) occur at only one stage.  Independence across coordinates therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E_U\{X_S(p_s)X_T(p_t)\}
=\min(p_s,p_t)^{|S\cap T|}p_s^{|S\setminus T|}p_t^{|T\setminus S|}.
\]
Subtracting \(\mathbb E_U X_S(p_s)\mathbb E_U X_T(p_t)=p_s^{|S|}p_t^{|T|}\) proves the displayed covariance formula, which is \(K_{st}(S,T)\) by Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}covariance\text{-}operator}\).

By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}low\text{-}order\text{-}schedule}\) and the definition of \(a\), finite summation over units yields
\[
M(r)=\bar c_{\varnothing}+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_SX_S(r),
\qquad
\bar c_{\varnothing}=\frac1n\sum_{i\in I_n}c_{i,\varnothing}.
\]
Consequently, Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}rollout\text{-}estimator}\) gives
\[
\widehat\tau_{p,w}
=\bar c_{\varnothing}\sum_{t=0}^kw_t
+\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}a_S\sum_{t=0}^kw_tX_S(p_t).
\]
The first term is nonrandom.  Bilinearity of covariance, the monomial identity just proved, and finiteness of \(\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
&=\sum_{S,T}a_Sa_T\sum_{s,t=0}^kw_sw_tK_{st}(S,T)\\
&=\sum_{S,T}a_SG(p,w)_{S,T}a_T
=a^{\mathsf T}G(p,w)a,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the second equality is Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}covariance\text{-}operator}\).  This proves both claims.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\sup_{(Y,c)\in\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)}\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{B^2}{n}\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}\max_{0\le h\le\beta}\lambda_{\max}\{H_h(p,w)\}=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
For every fixed \((p,w)\), if \(v^*\) is a unit leading eigenvector in an active block and \(Q_h\) is its explicit subset-lattice lift, then \(a^*=(B/\sqrt n)\Omega^{1/2}Q_hv^*\) attains the inner supremum. The schedule \(c^*_{i,S}=a^*_S\), \(c^*_{i,\varnothing}=0\), and \(Y_i^*(z)=\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}c^*_{i,S}\prod_{j\in S}z_j\) satisfies \(\max_{i\in I_n,z\in\{0,1\}^n}|Y_i^*(z)|\le\sum_{S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}}|a_S^*|<\infty\) and is a legal least-favourable member of \(\mathcal C_{n,\beta}(B,\omega)\). For fixed nodes \(p\), the weight problem has a semidefinite epigraph and attains its value after quotienting the common null directions of the covariance blocks.  The joint node--weight minimum is attained for every declared feasible tuple.
semantic_closure.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it solves Nature's exact common-uniform covariance problem, jointly minimizes over nodes and weights with guaranteed attainment, and produces the required legal converse schedule.
semantic_closure.gap: CortezEichhornYu2022 and the accepted Chebyshev-envelope proposal provide upper bounds without an attainable-covariance characterization or a joint-attainment proof; Kallus2021 provides an eigenvalue minimax template but not the nested subset kernel or rollout-node optimization.
semantic_closure.consumer: LinkedIn-style shared-hash ramps obtain a directly computable attained minimum and worst-case precision certificate under a declared interaction-strength budget.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every feasible \((n,\beta,k,q,\delta,B,\omega)\) with \(1\le\beta\le n\),
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}
=\min_{p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}}
\min_{w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w),
\]
and at least one joint minimizer exists.  For every fixed \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), the minimum over \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) is also attained.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
The feasibility conditions give \(k\ge\beta\), \(q>0\), and \(0<\delta\le q/k\).  Hence \(p_t=tq/k\) is feasible.  For any feasible \(p\), the nodes are distinct.  Let \(C(p)\) be the \((\beta+1)\)-by-\((k+1)\) matrix with entries \(C(p)_{d,t}=p_t^d\) for \(0\le d\le\beta\).  A row vector annihilating \(C(p)\) defines a polynomial of degree at most \(\beta\) vanishing at the \(k+1\ge\beta+1\) distinct nodes; it is therefore zero.  Thus \(C(p)\) has full row rank and
\[
C(p)w=(0,1,\ldots,1)^{\mathsf T}
\]
has a solution.  This is precisely an element of \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), so the joint feasible set is nonempty and the infimum is finite.

For a feasible pair define
\[
f(u)=\sum_{t=0}^kw_t\mathbf 1\{u\le p_t\},
\qquad
r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\quad(1\le j\le k).
\]
Degree-one exactness gives
\[
\int_0^1f(u)\,du=\sum_{t=0}^kw_tp_t=1.
\tag{46}
\]
Apart from finitely many endpoints, \(f=r_j\) on \((p_{j-1},p_j]\) and \(f=0\) on \((q,1]\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), the singleton case of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\), and (46) give, for every singleton \(S\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
G(p,w)_{S,S}
&=\operatorname{Var}\{f(U_i)\}\\
&=\int_0^1\{f(u)-1\}^2du\\
&=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)\\
&\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{47}
\]
Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}subset\text{-}lattice\text{-}block\text{-}reduction}\) and the singleton coordinate Rayleigh quotient therefore imply
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p,w)
\ge\frac{B^2\omega_1\delta}{n}
\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2.
\tag{48}
\]
The multiplier is strictly positive because \(B>0\), \(\omega_1>0\), \(n\ge1\), and \(\delta>0\).

Let \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\) be a joint minimizing sequence.  Its objective values are bounded, so (48) bounds every \(r_j^{(\ell)}\).  The identities
\[
w_k=r_k,
\qquad
w_j=r_j-r_{j+1}\ (1\le j<k),
\qquad
w_0=-r_1
\tag{49}
\]
where the last follows from \(\sum_tw_t=0\), then bound every coordinate of \(w^{(\ell)}\).  The node class is a closed and bounded finite-dimensional polytope, hence compact.  After taking a subsequence, \((p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})\to(p^*,w^*)\).  The endpoint equalities, spacing inequalities, and exactness equations are closed, so the limit is feasible.  The entries of \(G(p,w)\) are continuous because finite sums and products preserve continuity and \((x,y)\mapsto\min(x,y)\) is continuous.  The largest eigenvalue of a finite symmetric matrix is continuous.  Therefore
\[
V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^*,w^*)
=\lim_{\ell\to\infty}V_{\mathrm{rob}}(p^{(\ell)},w^{(\ell)})
=V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}.
\]
This proves joint attainment.  With \(p\) fixed, the same argument using (48)--(49) and the closed affine set \(\mathcal W_\beta(p)\) proves fixed-node attainment.
semantic_closure.justification: The first-moment singleton identity makes objective sublevels coercive in the weight coordinates, which turns compactness of the node polytope into joint attainment.
semantic_closure.gap: A spectral infimum alone does not certify that an implementable rollout attains it.
semantic_closure.consumer: The saddle theorem and the strict higher-order finite-stage barrier both require an attained design.

semantic_closure.statement: For the schedule in \(\text{def:quadratic-witness}\), \[\Gamma(u,v)=\operatorname{Cov}_U\{M(u),M(v)\}=\frac{\min(u,v)^2-u^2v^2}{9}.\] The nonbaseline interpolation weights are \(w_x=-\{x(1-2x)\}^{-1}\) and \(w_{1/2}=4(1-x)/(1-2x)\), and \[\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})=\frac{4(1-x)}{9(1-2x)}.\] This risk is strictly increasing on \([1/8,3/8]\), with values \(14/27\) at \(x=1/8\) and \(2/3\) at \(x=1/4\).
semantic_closure.justification: The witness verifies that exact shared-randomizer covariance changes the design criterion and that a familiar interior node need not dominate a more asymmetric node.
semantic_closure.gap: Published rollout bounds do not contain a legal finite-population example with a strict node-risk ordering generated by cross-stage covariance.
semantic_closure.consumer: A design reviewer can use this calculation as a regression test that implementation code has not silently replaced shared-hash stages by independent assignments.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Under Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}quadratic\text{-}witness}\),
\[
M(r)=\frac13Z_1(r)Z_2(r).
\]
By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}rollout}\), or by Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}uniform\text{-}monomial\text{-}covariance}\) with \(S=T=\{1,2\}\),
\[
\Gamma(u,v)=\frac19\{\min(u,v)^2-u^2v^2\}.
\tag{35}
\]
Let the weights at \(x\) and \(1/2\) be \(w_x\) and \(w_{1/2}\).  The degree-one and degree-two equations in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}unbiased\text{-}weight\text{-}class}\) are
\[
xw_x+\frac12w_{1/2}=1,
\qquad
x^2w_x+\frac14w_{1/2}=1.
\]
Their determinant is \(x(1-2x)/4>0\) for \(x\in[1/8,3/8]\), so their unique solution is
\[
w_x=-\frac1{x(1-2x)},
\qquad
w_{1/2}=\frac{4(1-x)}{1-2x}.
\tag{36}
\]
The remaining equation fixes \(w_0=-w_x-w_{1/2}\); it contributes no random term because \(M(0)=0\).

Using (35) at the three required pairs gives
\[
9\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=w_x^2(x^2-x^4)
+2w_xw_{1/2}\frac{3x^2}{4}
+w_{1/2}^2\frac3{16}.
\]
Substitution of (36) and collection over \((1-2x)^2\) give
\[
9\operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat\tau_{p,w})
=\frac{1-x^2-6x(1-x)+3(1-x)^2}{(1-2x)^2}
=\frac{4(1-x)}{1-2x}.
\]
Its derivative is
\[
\frac{d}{dx}\frac{4(1-x)}{9(1-2x)}
=\frac4{9(1-2x)^2}>0,
\]
so the risk is strictly increasing.  Direct evaluation gives \(14/27\) at \(x=1/8\) and \(2/3\) at \(x=1/4\), proving the proposition and verifying the smallest-instance common-uniform arithmetic.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every declared feasible tuple and every \(p\in\mathcal P_{k,q,\delta}\), \(w\in\mathcal W_\beta(p)\), define \(r_j=\sum_{t=j}^kw_t\).  For every singleton \(S\in\mathcal S_{n,\beta}\),
\[
G(p,w)_{S,S}=\sum_{j=1}^k(p_j-p_{j-1})(r_j-1)^2+(1-q)
\ge\delta\sum_{j=1}^k(r_j-1)^2
\quad\text{and}\quad
G(p,w)_{S,S}\ge\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
Consequently, if \(0<q<1\), then
\[
V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta}\ge
\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q}.
\]
At \(q=1\), \(V^*_{n,\beta,k,1,\delta}=0\), attained by \(w_0=-1\), \(w_k=1\), and zero intermediate weights.  If \(\beta=1\), then for every \(0<q\le1\),
\[
V^*_{n,1,k,q,\delta}=\frac{B^2\omega_1}{n}\frac{1-q}{q},
\]
and, for every fixed feasible \(p\), the unique minimizing weights are \(w_0=-1/q\), \(w_k=1/q\), and \(w_t=0\) for \(0<t<k\).
semantic_closure.justification: This is the sharp rollout-budget obstruction and its exact first-order solution; it also supplies the coercivity needed for joint node--weight attainment.
semantic_closure.gap: Spacing-only envelopes do not expose the exact support restriction induced by a common-uniform ramp or the resulting unique first-order readout.
semantic_closure.consumer: A rollout designer can read off the unavoidable precision loss from stopping at fraction \(q<1\), and can implement the unique optimal first-order weights.

semantic_closure.citation: Mayleen Cortez, Matthew Eichhorn, and Christina Lee Yu. Staggered Rollout Designs Enable Causal Inference Under Interference Without Network Knowledge. \emph{Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems}, 35, 2022. \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14552}.
